stories.headline: FBI Director Kash Patel gets engaged to longtime girlfriend, country singer Alexis Wilkins
stories.deck: Ms. Wilkins, 27, posted a black-and-white photo of herself standing with Mr. Patel, 46, flashing her hand in front of them to show off her ring
stories.bodyText:
FBI Director Kash Patel is engaged to his country singer girlfriend, Alexis Wilkins, the pair announced in a post to X on Sunday (October 4, 2026) evening.
Ms. Wilkins, 27, posted a black-and-white photo of herself standing with Mr. Patel, 46, flashing her hand in front of them to show off her ring with the caption, “Went and got the law involved.” The two have been dating since before Mr. Patel took over as head of the FBI in 2025, when she attended his swearing in.
The country singer and political commentator released her debut album in 2023. Ms. Wilkins has been affiliated with conservative groups and writes on her website that she “honours country tradition while adding relevance and current commentary.”
Mr. Patel, who reposted Ms. Wilkin's photo, has faced criticism for traveling on government aircraft on trips that have no known or apparent law enforcement purpose, including using an FBI jet to fly to State College, Pennsylvania, for a pro wrestling event where Ms. Wilkins performed the national anthem. Photos posted to social media by Ms. Wilkins afterward showed the couple smiling while she held an oversized golden championship belt.
Ms. Wilkins also made headlines as a performer at President Donald Trump's Great American State Fair on the National Mall as part of America 250, as other artists pulled out of the event after finding out it was not a non-partisan celebration.

stories.headline: Apple changes Mac OS after complaints over Meta’s AI agent accessing private data
stories.deck: Apple is set to roll out updates for its Mac operating system aimed at improving transparency regarding AI agent data access. These updates seek to enhance user privacy, especially due to worries surrounding Meta's AI agent Muse. Some developers have exploited 'Full Disk Access' in ways that could compromise user security and confidentiality.
stories.bodyText:
Apple is planning to change its Mac operating system, and the reason are AI Agents. The company wants to make it more clear to users when AI agents ask to access all of the data on their Macs. The announcement comes after some users have criticized Meta's Muse, an AI agent for accessing their private messages. While on Apple's iPhones and iPads, no single app can access data inside another app by default, company's Macs are more flexible. Apple Macs come with a 'Full Disk Access' option that allows apps such as cloud backup services to access all the data on a machine, with a user's permission.
In an update posted on its developer website, Apple said that some developers were using the Full Disk Access feature in ways that could put users at risk. "Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action," Apple wrote.
"As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially. We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy."
Apple's announcement comes after a technology columnist in Inc magazine accused Meta's Muse of reading private messages on his Mac. "In fact, I remember explicitly choosing not to let it have access to my messages, calendar, and other personal information," he wrote. He claimed that he had not enabled Full Disk Access and further added that when he asked Muse to explain how this occurred, the AI said that it was syncing his "device notifications." Similarly, a YouTuber named Matt Robb recently said that Muse mishandled a task in which he was selling things on Facebook Marketplace, leading to his address being shared.
Meta spokesperson Andy Stone disputed the claims saying that Muse's access to Apple's Messages app is strictly opt-in. "You have to enable both Full Disk Access and the Messages connector for Muse to be able to read your Messages content," Stone wrote on social media platform X, opens new tab. "It can't read your Messages unless you do this. And it can be revoked at any time."
Apple's complete statement on updates to Full Disk Access in macOS
"We give developers powerful APIs to build incredible capabilities into their apps for Apple products, backed by a set of controls designed to protect users’ private data. Full Disk Access largely sidesteps these controls in order to allow backup apps to function properly on the Mac. Some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems -- including files, mail, messages, and even browsing history -- without users’ full knowledge and understanding. For communication apps, this can also compromise the privacy of the people users are communicating with."
"Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action. Addressing this is critical. As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially. We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy."

stories.headline: 'Committed no wrong': BJP's Ravi Patil on form 7 SIR row
stories.deck: FIR over form 7: Ravi Patil says he committed no wrong
stories.bodyText: Belagavi: BJP leader Dr Ravi Patil appeared at the Market police station in Belagavi on Sunday for questioning in connection with an FIR over an alleged attempt to delete voter names from electoral rolls using Form 7 applications. . Speaking to reporters after appearing before the police, Dr Patil said, “I was summoned by the police for questioning. I have appeared before them. I have committed no wrong.” . “In Belagavi North Assembly constituency, I had submitted Form 7 and requested them to check the suspicious voters. I have not asked for the deletion of the votes of a particular community. We don’t have the power to do so. I have only objected to some confusion in the voters’ list. I have not done anything that will create tension in society,” said Dr Ravi Patil . Replying to a query, Dr Patil, “It was the BJP workers who submitted Form 7, and not the staff of my hospital and the allegations are false and concocted. .Case against BJP worker over form 7 to get voters deleted in Bengaluru's Malleswaram. A booth-level officer of the Ward 12 had filed a complaint against Dr Ravi Patil and others, alleging that they had attempted deleting 198 voters’ names from the electoral rolls using Form 7. . Dr Patil had unsuccessfully contested Belgaum Uttar on a BJP ticket in the 2023 Assembly elections. He had lost to Congress’ Asif Sait by a margin of around 3,000 votes.

stories.headline: Oil prices ease slightly as G7 and Middle East crude supplies set to hit market
stories.deck: Oil prices saw a modest decline as fresh shipments from the Middle East hit the market. The G7's move to tap into emergency reserves reflects growing energy apprehensions. Nevertheless, the crude oil market stays turbulent, as conflicts in the Gulf region persist. Notably, Yemen's Saudi-backed government has initiated a military operation against the Houthis, further complicating the situation.…
stories.bodyText:
Oil prices found marginal relief on Monday as concerns over global energy supplies eased with more crude entering the market. Additional shipments from the Middle East, along with the Group of Seven’s decision to release oil from emergency reserves, helped offset concerns over possible further damage to energy infrastructure in the Gulf amid the Iran war.
As of 7:15 am IST, Brent Crude was down 0.54% at $101.70 while WTI Crude fell 0.92% to $90.27.
The G7 agreement to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency stocks came last week, following pressure from US President Donald Trump. The countries also pledged not to impose energy export restrictions.
The G7 move comes as Middle Eastern crude exports have already picked up. Shipping data showed that exports were above pre-war levels on four of the seven days in the final week of September, despite attacks on vessels travelling through the Strait of Hormuz.
The market remains exposed to developments around the Gulf.
The Houthis said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area of Saudi Arabia, saying the attacks were in response to 50 Saudi-led air and missile strikes in Yemen over the previous 12 hours.
Yemen's Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government said on Sunday that it was beginning a major military campaign to retake all areas of the country controlled by the Iran-backed Houthis.
Aramco has also unexpectedly reduced its November crude oil prices for Asia to six-year lows, Reuters reported.
Meanwhile, OPEC+ has postponed a review that was expected to determine oil output quotas for its members in 2027. Two sources close to the matter said the US-Israeli war on Iran had disrupted projects intended to expand production capacity across the Middle East, making estimates of future production potential uncertain.
Developments in Europe are also shaping oil markets. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told Reuters that Ukraine would step up attacks on Russian oil refineries.
Brent had surrendered most of its gains from the previous week, while WTI was 1.6% lower after the G7 decision.
As the Middle East conflict stretches beyond the seven-month mark, the oil market has remained volatile. However, while prices have continued to rise broadly, the latest gains remain well below the spike seen earlier in the conflict, when crude touched $126 per barrel.

stories.headline: Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro beats polls in presidential vote, faces Lula in runoff
stories.deck: The two leading candidates will advance ‌to the second round of voting on October 25
stories.bodyText:
Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro will face President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in the runoff of a presidential election, the country’s electoral authority said on Sunday (October 4, 2026).
With just over 97% of the ballots counted, the right-wing challenger took 47.45% of valid votes in the first round, beating the forecasts in most private surveys. Leftist Lula received 44.66% of the votes.
The two leading candidates will advance to the second round of voting on October 25, beating out a field of 12 candidates in a campaign focused on concerns about the growing cost of living, corruption and insecurity in Brazilians’ daily lives.
Mr. Flavio, the 45-year-old son of former President Jair Bolsonaro who hopes to return his father’s right-wing movement to power, was leading leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva (80), who is seeking a fourth term, following a campaign dominated by corruption scandals, economic anxiety and accusations of U.S. meddling.
Analysts told Reuters they believed Mr. Flavio was receiving “protest votes” of people voting against Mr. Lula rather than for the right-wing senator — votes they had been expected to save until a second round.
A victory for the senator would extend a wave of wins across Latin America by right-wing candidates aligned with U.S. President Donald Trump, while Lula’s reelection could create a headache for Washington, which has clashed with his government over trade and security.
Despite growing worries over Brazil’s public finances and sluggish economic growth, the campaign offered meager policy debate, as both leading candidates skipped the major TV debates.
Undecided voters
Mr. Flavio told journalists in Rio de Janeiro he was confident he could win the presidency in the first round, citing voters’ frustration with his chief opponent.
Mr. Flavio was counting on “a protest vote from people who would otherwise vote for another candidate but are opposed to Mr. Lula,” he said. “I hope it’s enough to secure a victory in the first round.”
Thaise Lima, a 41-year-old lawyer on her way to vote in Sao Paulo, said her main goal was to get Mr. Lula’s Workers’ Party out of office.
“I don’t think Flavio is the best candidate, but I might decide to vote for him in the next few minutes,” she said, adding that she wished psychiatrist and author Augusto Cury were a more viable candidate.
Fernando Tempel, 49, a management consultant, told Reuters he was voting for Flavio despite initially planning to vote for Romeu Zema, the former governor of Minas Gerais state.
Outside interference
On the other hand, Mr. Lula’s allies have warned that the Trump administration might refuse to recognize election results if he wins, pointing to an aborted effort to send U.S. officials to Brazil.
“What is at stake is the future of Brazil,” Mr. Lula said after voting in Sao Bernardo do Campo, in Sao Paulo state.
Mr. Trump has not formally endorsed a candidate, though he hosted Senator Flavio Bolsonaro at the White House and praised him publicly.
“I’m a little worried about everything that’s been happening recently, including internationally. I feel this election has had a lot of outside influence, more than in previous elections,” said Cristiano, 34, a doctor in Brasilia who voted for Lula and preferred to withhold his surname.
“We are confident in our President Lula, who will fight for national sovereignty,” said Pedro Palacio, 45, who was voting in Brasilia alongside his wife, Andreia, and their two sons and two dogs, all of whom wore outfits supporting the President.
As of Sunday (October 4, 2026) afternoon, the election was proceeding normally, Brazil’s electoral court chief Kassio Nunes Marques said in a press conference.
“Teams monitoring international risks have not identified any risks whatsoever,” he said.
Reuters reported on Wednesday that Brazilian intelligence officials briefed a French and German delegation on alleged U.S. and Russian interference before the election. The U.S. has rejected claims of interference in Brazil’s affairs.
Economic headwinds
Despite falling inequality and unemployment, Mr. Lula has struggled to win over voters grappling with high living costs, heavy household debt and the threat of street crime and more pervasive gang activity.
Flavio Bolsonaro has sought to capitalize on cost-of-living concerns, while Mr. Lula has moved to ban online gambling and, as the race tightened, expanded welfare and proposed fresh debt relief for families.
Rising spending and public debt above 82% of GDP have stoked fiscal concerns that Brazil’s next President will need to address. The government lowered its economic growth forecasts for this year and next to 2.0% and 2.3% respectively.
“I voted for Brazil to start growing again,” said Marciano de Souza e Silva, a 52-year-old public servant in Brasilia and former Mr. Lula voter who moved right, voting for Jair Bolsonaro in 2018 and 2022 and Mr. Flavio on Sunday (October 4, 2026).
“The best social program is one that encourages people to start businesses, to actually produce real wealth,” he said.
Scandal-plagued campaigns
Overshadowing the policy debate, a scandal surrounding the now-defunct Banco Master has engulfed much of Brazil’s political class and renewed public anger over corruption.
Daniel Vorcaro, who ran the bank, was arrested earlier this year and accused of a multibillion-dollar fraud scheme. The investigation has probed the banker’s ties to figures from Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to Flavio Bolsonaro, who is being investigated for money laundering tied to the case by the federal police.
The candidate has denied any wrongdoing, although he confirmed raising millions of dollars from Mr. Vorcaro to make a movie about his father.
The banker’s connections to Mr. Moraes, widely perceived as a Mr. Lula ally, plunged the court into crisis a month before the vote, creating fresh problems for the President. Mr. Moraes has said the case against him is politically motivated for his role in the conviction of the elder Mr. Bolsonaro.
On Sunday (October 4, 2026), voters will also elect all 513 lower house members and two-thirds of the Senate, where some lawmakers have pushed to impeach Mr. Moraes.
Congress has gained greater influence in Brazilian politics since the impeachment of former President Dilma Rousseff, a Lula ally, in 2016, raising the stakes of those legislative races.

briefs.headline: Saudi-backed govt launches military drive to retake Houthi-held territory
briefs.deck: In a bold move to reclaim territory from the Houthis, Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi has announced new military operations. These efforts focus on consolidating state authority throughout Yemen, especially around the besieged city of Taiz, where access routes have been blocked. As tensions rise, Saudi Arabia's involvement has intensified with missile strikes, further threatening both regional…
briefs.bodyText:
Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi on Sunday announced the launch of military operations to retake territory held by the Iran-backed Houthis, declaring that government forces would seek to restore state authority across the country.
“Today, I announce the start of military operations to retake the remaining territory of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory,” Al-Alimi said in a televised address, according to the BBC.
The announcement followed a major Houthi offensive last month, during which the Iran-backed group seized territory along Yemen's Red Sea coastline, including areas around the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait. The Houthis have also continued to advance around Taiz, a key government-held city in southwestern Yemen.
The escalation has also brought 
Saudi Arabia
 directly into the latest phase of the conflict. The Houthis claimed they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area, saying the attacks were carried out in response to 50 Saudi-led coalition strikes in Yemen over 12 hours.
“Both operations successfully achieved their objectives,” Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said, according to the BBC.
The immediate battlefield focus is Taiz, where the Houthis have reportedly cut a vital supply route linking the city with Aden, the interim capital of the Yemeni government.
AFP, citing three Yemeni military sources, reported that the move has effectively left Taiz surrounded.
“They've achieved the military objective of isolating Taiz from Aden, even if they haven't fully taken control of it,” Farea Al-Muslimi, a research fellow at Chatham House, told AFP.
Government and Saudi-led coalition forces have been targeting Houthi military positions as the government seeks to weaken the group before attempting to reclaim territory.
The latest escalation comes against the backdrop of Yemen's war, which began in 2014 when the Houthis seized Sanaa and expanded their control across northern Yemen. Saudi Arabia intervened the following year at the head of a coalition supporting the internationally recognised government.
The Houthis' latest offensive has now altered the battlefield, giving them greater control of Yemen's Red Sea coastline and increasing their leverage over the Bab al-Mandab shipping route.
The developments also pose a direct risk to Saudi Arabia's oil infrastructure. Any sustained Houthi campaign against Saudi energy facilities could have wider consequences for global oil markets, while Houthi control or disruption around Bab al-Mandab could threaten one of the world's key maritime trade routes.

briefs.headline: Case against BJP worker over form 7 to get voters deleted in Bengaluru's Malleswaram
briefs.deck: Case against BJP worker over form 7 to get voters deleted in Malleswaram
briefs.bodyText: BENGALURU: Bengaluru police have registered an FIR following allegations of irregularities related to the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in the Malleswaram Assembly constituency, officials said on Sunday. . The FIR was registered against G S Vasanthalakshmi - believed to be associated with the BJP - on October 2 based on a complaint from Anoop Iyengar, a Congress leader. . Police have invoked BNS sections 319(2) (cheating by personation), 336(2) (forgery), 340(2) (forged document or electronic record and using it as genuine), 61(2)(b) (criminal conspiracy) and 217(b) (false information, with intent to cause public servant to use his lawful power to injury of another person). . Iyengar told the police that at polling stations in Ward 64, he was informed that Form 7 applications were submitted showing voters as persons who had shifted residence or were otherwise ineligible to be on the electoral rolls. This was an attempt to get their names deleted from the electoral rolls, he stated, accused Vasanthalakshmi of being involved. .'A legal provision...': Karnataka BJP urges police chief to stop booking party workers over submission of Form 7. According to the FIR, 778 voter entries were spread across different polling stations: 122 applications in polling station 157, 233 in polling station 155, 28 in 156, five in 158, 47 in 154, 171 in 205, 68 in 203 and 104 applications in polling station 153. . Anyone can file Form 7 to get names deleted from the electoral rolls during the SIR.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru: Senior citizen’s land restored after fake deed fraud; two arrested
briefs.deck: Senior citizen’s land restored after fake deed fraud; two arrested
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: The Lokayukta has intervened in a case involving the alleged fraudulent transfer of an 84-year-old woman’s land in Devanahalli taluk, leading to the arrest of two people, filing of a chargesheet and restoration of her name in revenue records. . Lokayukta officials said the land belonging to Bharathi L Reddy of Chikkatattamangala village in Vijayapura hobli comprises three acres in Survey No 95/1, one acre and 25 guntas in Survey No 94/1, and one acre and eight guntas in Survey No 92/2. . A fake gift deed was registered at the Hoskote Sub-Registrar’s Office on August 13, 2025, by impersonating Bharathi. The properties were subsequently transferred in the name of her son, Shravan Kumar. Bharathi lodged a complaint with the Lokayukta on October 23, 2025, after learning of the fraud. . During a hearing on October 3, Lokayukta Justice BS Patil questioned the officials concerned about the action taken and directed them to submit a report. .B M Kaval land grab case: Mudigere police arrest man; probe underway.KIADB likely to approve Rs 2.7 crore per acre for Devanahalli farmers. Vijayapura police subsequently arrested Lakshmi Devamma, who impersonated Bharathi, and Shravan Kumar, the beneficiary of the fraudulent deed. The investigating officer informed the Lokayukta that the investigation was complete and a chargesheet had been filed before the court. . Meanwhile, the Doddaballapur sub-divisional officer, through an order dated August 12 this year, directed the restoration of Bharathi’s name in the revenue records after the fraudulent deed led to its removal. Her name has since been restored as the owner. . Taking serious note of similar cases involving the fraudulent takeover of senior citizens’ properties, the Lokayukta directed the Inspector General of Registration and the Principal Secretary of the Revenue Department to submit a report on preventive and punitive measures to curb such frauds.

briefs.headline: Man, two grandchildren drown in agricultural pond in Chickballapur
briefs.deck: The Chintamani Rural Police visited the spot and conducted an initial inspection. The bodies were subsequently recovered from the pond and shifted to the Chintamani Government Hospital mortuary for post-mortem.
briefs.bodyText:
Tragedy struck Husenapura village in Chintamani taluk of Chickballapur district on Saturday when a 60-year-old man and his two grandchildren drowned in an agricultural pond. The deceased have been identified as Muninarayanappa, and Ashwin, 10, and Prajwal, 11.
According to family members, Muninarayanappa used to visit the Anjaneya Swamy temple located on his land every Saturday. On Saturday morning, he left home for the temple along with his two grandchildren.
When they did not return by evening, concerned relatives tried contacting them over the phone, but received no response. Family members and villagers subsequently began searching the surrounding agricultural fields.
During the search, the bodies of the three were found floating in an agricultural pond belonging to a farmer identified as Ashwathappa, near the temple. The family immediately informed the police.
The Chintamani Rural Police visited the spot and conducted an initial inspection. The bodies were subsequently recovered from the pond and shifted to the Chintamani Government Hospital mortuary for post-mortem.
Preliminary suspicion is that the two children may have accidentally slipped into the water while playing near the pond. Muninarayanappa may have entered the pond in an attempt to rescue them but was unable to save them due to the depth of the water, it is suspected.
The family has also raised the possibility of an electrical accident, as electricity wires and a pump set are reportedly located near the agricultural pond.

stories.headline: A Night of Wonderment: AR Rahman gives Bengaluru a musical spectacle to remember
stories.bodyText:
When you sign up for a concert by a music maestro, you often sign up for the long wait too: hours of anticipation, a late start, tired feet and a weary journey home. But on Saturday night, Bengaluru was in for a pleasant surprise.
AR Rahman returned to the city after eight years, and Laughing water entertainment and Noise & grains present AR Rahman The Wonderment Tour Bengaluru, which opened its 2026 India leg at KTPO Grounds in Whitefield, began remarkably on time. Then came nearly three hours of music that never once let the energy dip. For an audience that had waited so long to see one of India’s most celebrated composers live again, the night was worth every moment, every mile and every penny.
A star-studded musical ensemble
The setlist travelled from Tamil and Hindi hits to a surprise Kannada rendition of the beloved 
Roja
 song, with an engaging jugalbandi between his musicians along the way. Rahman was joined on stage by singers 
Vijay Prakash
, Jonita Gandhi, Rakshita Suresh, AR Ameen, Adithya RKay, Heer, Nitesh Aher, Raghav Kaushik and others, while musicians including Ranjit Barot, Ashwin Srinivasan, Evelyn Soto, Nilanjana Ghosh, Rangappriya Sankaranarayanan, Haritha Raj and Aleif Hamdan added to the musical spectacle.
The audience was all heart
The evening began on a high. The sound was rich, the visuals striking, and Rahman’s presence drew roars from a packed crowd. Familiar melodies rolled out one after another, thousands of voices rose as one, and phone lights swayed in unison.
There were a few hiccups too: some singers drifted off beat, pre-recorded tracks were noticeable, and the setlist had its share of lesser-known songs. But Bengaluru took it all in good spirit. The crowd had come for Rahman and his music, and they were happy to sing along, cheer the performers and soak in the evening.
‘Bengaluru recognised the music before anyone else did’
Speaking about his early memories of the city, Rahman began in Kannada: “
Enu, maja madtha idira?
 (Are you having fun?)”
“I was working with composers like Vijay Anand, and that’s when I first came to Bengaluru, back in 1987,” he said. “But in 1995, when 
Rangeela
 released, I came here for some other work and the film’s music was playing everywhere. You guys recognised what music is. Everybody said it wouldn’t work, but when I heard it playing everywhere in Bengaluru, I was like, ‘Okay, this is going to work.’ That’s when I knew it was a hit.”

stories.headline: Three of family drown in farm pond in Karnataka
stories.bodyText:
Chintamani: A 60-year-old man and his two grandchildren drowned in a farm pond at Hussianpura village near Ambajidurga in Chintamani taluk of Chikkaballapur district Saturday.
The deceased were identified as Muninarayanappa, 60, and his grandchildren Yashwin, 7, and 
Prajwal
, 8, all residents of Hussianpura.
A devotee of Sri Hanuman, Muninarayanappa regularly visited a temple near the village on Saturdays for the abhisheka ritual. He left home for the temple on Saturday morning with his grandchildren. When the three failed to return by evening, family members began searching for them.
They later found their bodies floating in a Krushi honda (farm pond) near the temple.
Police suspect the children may have fallen into the pond while playing, prompting Muninarayanappa to enter the water in an attempt to rescue them. However, he may have been unable to get out due to the slippery conditions.
Family members alleged that the pond, which belongs to a villager, lacked protective fencing, contributing to the tragedy.

stories.headline: Nearly 30% of Karnataka’s waterbodies used mainly to recharge groundwater
stories.deck: Karnataka has the second-highest share among the major southern States, after Tamil Nadu
stories.bodyText:
Nearly 30% of Karnataka’s waterbodies are being used mainly to recharge groundwater, according to the Union Ministry of Jal Shakti’s Second Census of Water Bodies.
Of the 28,075 waterbodies currently in use in the State, 8,353 are primarily used for this purpose, Minor Irrigation and Science and Technology Minister Ajay Dharma Singh said on Sunday.
Karnataka has the second-highest share among the major southern States, after Tamil Nadu. In Tamil Nadu, 34.3% of waterbodies are primarily used for groundwater recharge, followed by Karnataka at 29.8%, Telangana at 27.5%, Andhra Pradesh at 19.2% and Kerala at 15.3%.
Mr. Singh said that it is not about comparing performances of the States, but recharging groundwater was important for Karnataka as the State often faces drought and uneven rainfall. Lakes, tanks and other waterbodies help rainwater seep into the ground and replenish groundwater, he said. “The waterbodies are not just storage structures, they are systems that help secure our groundwater for the future,” he said.
About 96% of Karnataka’s waterbodies are in rural areas. Their condition and ability to recharge groundwater are therefore important for farming, drinking water, livestock and other needs in rural areas, Mr. Singh added.
Of the 8,353 waterbodies primarily used for groundwater recharge, 5,302 are classified as waterbodies, 1,548 as lakes and 1,267 as ponds, the census data showed.
Mr. Singh said the State government would focus on measures such as protecting watersheds, removing silt from waterbodies, restoring lakes and promoting rainwater harvesting along with groundwater management. Strengthening the ability of rural waterbodies to recharge groundwater would be a priority, he said.

stories.headline: 500 students join Bengaluru run to open up conversations on mental health
stories.bodyText:
More than 2,000 people, including around 500 school students, participated in the World Mental Health Day Run at Cubbon Park in central Bengaluru on Sunday, ahead of World Mental Health Day on October 10.
The youth-led initiative was organised by Imaan Zara Khan, a Grade 11 student at a private school in the city, and a 1M1B Changemaker. The event featured 3K, 5K and 10K runs and brought together students and runners in the city to encourage conversations around emotional well-being among young people.
The 3K category titled “Unspoken Run” carried the message, “A step for every conversation we never had,” with participants encouraged to see the run as part of a larger effort to make conversations around mental health easier to begin.
The event was part of Project S.A.F.E. (Student Advocacy for Emotional Well-Being), a student-led initiative founded by Imaan that focuses on adolescent mental health through research, storytelling and systems-level advocacy.
The initiative examines how signs of distress among young people are recognised, how they seek help, how adults respond and how schools can create clearer pathways to appropriate support.
“Through S.A.F.E., I want to move the conversation beyond awareness and ask a harder question: when a young person is struggling, what happens next? Who recognises the signs, who responds, and how do they reach the right support?” Imaan said.
Imaan will next present Project S.A.F.E. at the 10th 1M1B Summit at the United Nations Office in Geneva, where she will join youth leaders, institutions and stakeholders from across the world.

briefs.headline: Citizens get private land for road widening, Nallurhalli traffic to ease in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A longstanding traffic bottleneck on Nallurhalli Temple Road is set to ease after a private landowner agreed to allow public use of a portion of his property.
The bottleneck was caused by a roughly 40-metre-long section where the carriageway narrowed significantly as part of the road fell within privately-owned land. While the road remained relatively wide on either side of the stretch, the narrowed segment forced traffic from both directions through a constricted space, creating daily congestion for residents, motorists and school buses.
After nearly a year of discussions, citizen collective Whitefield Rising secured permission from the landowner to use the portion of land for road purposes. Residents clarified that ownership of the land remains with the individual and that there has been no transfer or relinquishment of title.
Following the agreement, Whitefield Rising mobilised a crowdfunding campaign and raised Rs 4 lakh to asphalt the section. Road-widening work was taken up Sunday.
Residents said the newly-asphalted stretch will remain closed for about two weeks for curing before being opened to public traffic.
East City Corporation was unavailable for comment.
“This junction has .been a problem irrespective of the time of day. Whether during peak hours or otherwise, the narrow road causes congestion for commuters travelling between Nallurhalli and Whitefield,” said Rahul, a resident of Nallurhalli
“Had this gone through regular govt processes, resolving and widening the stretch could have taken several more years. 
The owner’s decision to allow public use of the land has helped address a major bottleneck,” said Zibi Jamal, from Whitefield Rising.
“Govt cannot do everything. Residents can play a role in solving local issues too. However, there are certain infrastructure challenges that only govt agencies can address. This initiative is a good example of citizens stepping up while continuing to seek support for larger mobility solutions,” said Aravind Kirthi, another resident of Nallurhalli.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru techie drowns in quarry during Instagram-group trek; body found after 2-day search
briefs.deck: A holiday trek organized through an Instagram group ended tragically when Ganesh Anjaneya Vinay drowned in a quarry. Vinay, who was 30 years old, had been swimming with a group when he suddenly disappeared. Despite attempts by group members to rescue him, they were unsuccessful, prompting a search by local authorities. After two days of searching, rescuers recovered his body from the water-filled…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A holiday trek, organised through an Instagram group, ended in tragedy after a 30-year-old techie allegedly drowned in a water-filled stone quarry near Yellammanadoddi, close to Jigani, on Oct 2.
His body was recovered Sunday morning, following a two-day search operation.
The deceased, Ganesh Anjaneya Vinay, a resident of Halasuru, belonged to Vijayawada in Andhra Pradesh.
According to the preliminary investigation, Vinay worked as an associate UX designer for a private firm in Bengaluru. Vinay, who had a master’s degree from IIT Delhi, was living in Bengaluru for the past four years.
Vinay had joined a group of eight trekkers for the outing during the Gandhi Jayanti holiday weekend. Among those who joined the trek was Vinay’s fiancé, a veterinary doctor.
During the outing, the group stopped at a huge stone quarry near Yellammanadoddi. Mining activity at the quarry had reportedly stopped around 15 years ago, and the abandoned pit had since filled with water. The group decided to swim in the quarry.
What happened
According to police, the group members took a dive and were enjoying themselves when, at around 5.30pm, Vinay suddenly disappeared in the water.
The other members tried to rescue him, but were unsuccessful. They alerted Jigani police, who rushed to the spot along with personnel from the fire and emergency services.
Police and rescue teams searched the quarry and subsequently summoned personnel from State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) and National Disaster Response Force (
NDRF
), besides involving local divers in the operation.
Jigani police later contacted Eshwar Malpe, a scuba diver known for undertaking underwater rescue operations, and his team from Malpe for assistance. After nearly two days of continuous efforts, rescuers finally located Vinay’s body around 9am Sunday.
Based on a complaint filed by Vinay’s brother, Jigani police registered an unnatural death report (UDR).
The trekking group had connected with each other through Instagram and had planned the trek through the social media group, a senior officer said. The Instagram account regularly shares details about trekking destinations on the outskirts of Bengaluru and in neighbouring districts.
According to the members, they had been swimming for around one-and-a-half hours before Vinay drowned.
What was meant to be a holiday trek and an adventurous outing ended in tragedy, leaving the group and Vinay’s family traumatised.

briefs.headline: SIR: BJP BLA sought Form-7 deletions, verification against 7,561 names in Ballari; FIR registered
briefs.deck: The FIR, the sixth in Karnataka regarding misuse of Form-7, was registered at the Brucepet police station on October 1, after a complaint by a Congress BLA Goutham S.
briefs.bodyText:
Claiming that more than 7,500 electors were either “absent or had shifted,” a BJP-affiliated Booth Level Agent (BLA) attempted to first fill Form-7 applications and, after his claims were not accepted by the election authorities, again sought “revision” of their names by submitting objections, even though these electors figured in the draft electoral roll of Ballari City Assembly constituency.
In this regard, an FIR, the sixth in Karnataka regarding misuse of Form-7 (seeking deletions), was registered at the Brucepet police station on October 1 after a Congress BLA complained that T. Srinivas Mothkur, Opposition leader of Ballari City Corporation, also the BJP BLA-1, had sought deletion of the names of 7,561 electors. The FIR books the accused under Section 353 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, for “statements conducing to public mischief”.
Of the previous five FIRs, three including two in Belagavi and one in Mysuru, named BJP members as accused.
Repeated attempts
The FIR followed a series of attempts by Mr. Mothkur to submit the objections. On September 21, he wrote to the Ballari City Corporation saying that while he was trying to submit Form-7 applications through the BLOs concerned, many BLOs had refused to accept them and only a few had accepted them. He then took the remaining applications directly to the ERO, saying they related to booths where the BLOs had refused to accept them.
In its response the same day, election authorities from the Ballari City Corporation said Mr. Mothkur’s claims that the voters were already registered elsewhere, absent or permanently shifted “were not supported” by documents or other information. The ERO said that while BLAs were allowed to submit applications in bulk, they could submit no more than 10 applications to a BLO at a time or in a day. If a BLA submitted more than 30 applications during the claims and objections period, the ERO or AERO had to personally cross-verify them. The BLA was also required to submit a list of the applications along with a declaration that he had personally verified the particulars and was satisfied that they were correct, the ERO’s letter said.
Following this response, Mr. Mothkur made another attempt the following day. On September 22, he wrote to the election authorities saying that he was ready to submit objections against 7,561 voters in the draft electoral roll of Ballari City Assembly constituency. He enclosed the list of names and sought necessary action and completion of the revision of the electoral roll “at the earliest.” The election authorities again denied, arguing that it was not possible to verify the voters’ registration merely on the basis of the complaint.
Complaint and clarification
The repeated attempts to seek deletion of the names led to a complaint by Congress BLA Goutham S. He alleged that Mr. Mothkur had submitted Form-7 applications against the 7,561 electors and that at some polling stations, election officials had re-verified the names based on his objections. He also alleged that the majority of the names belonged to a minority community and that the BJP BLA was attempting to remove minority voters from the electoral roll.
Speaking to The Hindu, Mr. Mothkur said that, as BLA-1, he had asked the BLA-2 to identify voters who had shifted or were absent and provide him with a list. The BLA-2 had identified the voters and the list was submitted to the ERO for verification, he said. He said he had neither sought deletion of their names nor claimed that the information was correct, but had only provided the details for the ERO to verify.

NEW DELHI: Honda Motorcycle and Scooter India (HMSI) expects a stronger festive season than last year, but rising material costs are putting pressure on profitability, president and CEO Tsutsumu Otani told TOI.
The company is seeing growth alongside an expanding motorcycle market, with dealers anticipating robust festive demand. However, Otani said the situation in West Asia was pushing up material costs, complicating the profitability outlook despite favourable business conditions.

Honda is preparing inventory to meet festive demand across regions. Otani said business had been growing month by month, although the improvement in demand was accompanied by pressure on costs.

stories.headline: EY India chief seeks easier GST refunds, tax credits
stories.deck: EY India chairman Rajiv Memani emphasized the importance of expediting GST refunds and addressing input tax credit issues. He suggested allowing companies to claim expenses related to travel and insurance as eligible credits. Memani highlighted the successful impact of recent GST reforms on India's economic growth. He projected FDI flows could exceed $100 billion this year, which may double in…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The GST Council should speed up refunds and address issues around accumulation of input tax credit, including for services and capital goods, while also allowing companies to take credit for expenses related to travel and insurance, EY India chairman & CEO Rajiv Memani said ahead of Wednesday's meeting.
Several of these issues are expected to be addressed by the all-powerful body, led by Union finance minister 
Nirmala Sitharaman
.
"GST 2.0 has been reasonably successful. Right now, we should look at how you can make GST more user-friendly. GST refunds, audits should be simplified as companies are having multiple audits, which should be consolidated at the central level," Memani said, while adding decriminalisation and easing of filing to his wish list of reforms.
Memani suggested that govt also needs to address issues related to direct tax disputes as part of efforts to step up FDI inflows
The head of EY India, which provides tax advisory services to leading names in the corporate sector, said that the rate and process rationalisation initiative taken last Sept was highly successful.
"You're seeing good growth in India relative to other parts of the world is due to the reforms that have been undertaken. The most significant, tangible impact has been from GST reforms," he said, arguing that the growth in consumer goods, automobiles has been powered by rate cuts and procedural simplification.
"You look at sector by sector, the reform has really played out very well. From a consumption standpoint, it has resulted in more hiring, private capex has been higher, and it has also helped direct tax collections grow faster. GST revenue growth will be significantly higher (than what was targeted). It's a very strong endorsement that if you have simpler rules, if you moderate the tax rates, there is positive impact on the economy."
Memani suggested that govt also needs to address issues related to direct tax disputes as part of efforts to step up FDI inflows. He also said that inter-ministerial approach to resolving issues flagged by large investors can boost inflows.
"We can cross $100 billion FDI this year and double that in three years. The opportunity is humongous." Citing feedback from companies, he said India was in a sweet spot with high growth at a time when global corporations are looking at "strategic diversification" with India's FTAs also expected to attract investors. Besides, he said, sectors such as space, defence and electronics are more open to overseas investment.
FDI flows were estimated at around $97 billion in 2025-26 and grew 12.5% to $43.9 billion during April-July, according to RBI data.

stories.headline: Next-Gen GST and India’s next phase of growth
stories.deck: Next-Gen GST was conceived with two connected purposes: to reduce and rationalise rates, and to make compliance easier
stories.bodyText:
India’s ambition to become a Viksit Bharat requires an economy in which enterprises of every size can grow, wherever they begin. Over the past 12 years, our government has worked to create those conditions. The introduction of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in 2017 established a common national framework for indirect taxation. Next-Gen GST carries that effort forward, drawing on nine years of implementation and the experience of taxpayers and States.
Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision, Next-Gen GST was conceived with two connected purposes: to reduce and rationalise rates, and to make compliance easier. The rate changes took effect on September 22, 2025. The next phase of process reforms will come before the GST Council shortly. Together, these efforts seek to give households relief, businesses greater certainty and taxpayers a system in which they can fulfil their obligations without avoidable difficulty.

stories.headline: Experts’ poll: RBI may hike rates by 0.25% in October policy amid inflationary pressures
stories.deck: The last repo rate hike was in February 2023, when the RBI raised the rate by 0.25% to 6.50%
stories.bodyText:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is likely to increase the repo rate by 0.25% in the October monetary policy review due to mounting inflationary pressure amid the re-escalation of the West Asia crisis and also the rate hikes by global central banks, according to economists and bankers.
If the RBI increases the rate in the upcoming policy, it would mark a reversal in the interest rate policy, which has witnessed rate cuts in 2025 and an extended pause thereafter, according to a PTI poll of 16 economists and bankers.
The last repo rate hike was in February 2023, when the RBI raised the rate by 0.25% to 6.50%; it then kept the rate unchanged through 2023-24 before beginning its rate-cut cycle in 2025. Currently, the RBI's policy repo rate stands at 5.25%.
"Coordination with global central bank hikes, rising inflation risks and strong growth momentum provide policy space to hike," said Kanika Pasricha, Chief Economic Advisor at Union Bank of India.
Further, Dipti Deshpande, principal economist at Crisil, said that since the last policy, inflationary pressures have mounted further mainly due to the re-escalation of the West Asia conflict and the pressure on energy and commodity prices. If these pressures persist, further rate hikes are expected.
A majority of participants in the PTI poll expect a rate hike with a hawkish tone at the upcoming policy review on Wednesday (October 7, 2026). The opinion seems divided on whether there will be a shift in stance.
Sachchidanand Shukla, group chief economist at Larsen & Toubro, however, feels that the RBI will again opt for status quo.
He reasoned that the RBI could wait before raising rates, as there is no evidence yet of demand-led inflation or overheating in the economy.
On the number of rate hikes expected in FY27, experts broadly see at least two increases, with several expecting two to three hikes over the course of the fiscal.
Experts said the RBI may need to gradually normalise its monetary policy stance as headline inflation rises, requiring a rate hike to ensure real interest rates do not turn negative in the coming quarters.
"Gradual normalisation of policy as headline inflation is higher. The rate hike is needed to ensure real rates are not negative in the coming quarters," said Gaura Sengupta, economist at IDFC First Bank.
On the policy stance, experts are divided between 'no change' and 'calibrated tightening', with some also favouring 'withdrawal of accommodation'.
On the policy tone, however, a majority of experts expect a hawkish stance, while a few see the tone as cautious, reflecting concerns over rising inflation and global rate movements.
The experts expect an upward revision to the RBI's FY27 CPI inflation forecast amid elevated crude oil prices, food inflation risks and broadening price pressures.
"The recent surge in crude oil prices to above $100/barrel could likely lead to an increase in the retail selling price (RSP) of petrol and diesel, and further generalisation of price pressures, which would necessitate an upward revision in the CPI inflation forecasts," said Aditi Nayar, chief economist, head-research and outreach at ICRA.
Apoorva Javadekar, chief economist at Shriram Group, said there will be a mild upward revision of 0.10% for Q3 and Q4 of FY27. "In fact, the upward revision to future inflation is almost a pre-condition for a rate hike, as otherwise the inflation is progressing on the projected path."
Rajani Sinha, chief economist at Careedge Ratings, said price pressures are becoming increasingly broad-based, with "around 19% of the 358 items in the CPI basket" recording inflation above 6% in August, up from 13% in March.
India's retail inflation accelerated to an eight-month high of 4.82% in August from 4.45% in July. CPI inflation has stayed above the RBI's 4% target for three straight months, climbing from 3.93% in May to 4.38% in June and 4.45% in July. The August print marked the highest level recorded so far under the new CPI series, which uses 2024 as its base year.
In August monetary policy, the Central bank projected CPI inflation for FY27 at 5.0% with Q2 at 4.7%, Q3 at 5.9%, and Q4 at 5.5%. Inflation for Q1:2027-28 is projected at 5.3%. Core inflation was projected at 4.3% for 2026-27.
On growth, experts largely expect the RBI to revise its FY27 GDP growth forecast upwards, with stronger-than-expected economic activity in the first half of the fiscal supporting the outlook, although some expect no change.
Radhika Rao, Senior Economist and Executive Director at DBS Bank, expects a "slight upward revision to above 7% growth".
The Central bank in its August monetary policy projected real GDP growth for 2026-27 at 6.7%, with Q1 at 7.0%, Q2 at 6.4%, Q3 at 6.5%, and Q4 at 6.8%. Real GDP growth for Q1:2027-28 was projected at 7.3%.
On liquidity management, experts expect the RBI to continue using variable rate reverse repo (VRRR) operations, open market operations (OMOs) and foreign exchange swap operations to absorb surplus liquidity from the banking system.

briefs.headline: Credit offtake stays ahead of banks' deposit growth
briefs.deck: In the second quarter of FY27, advances at several banks grew significantly faster than deposit growth. Smaller banks, such as Tamilnad Mercantile Bank and Karnataka Bank, recorded impressive credit expansions. Larger public sector banks like Bank of India and Canara Bank also saw substantial growth in advances. However, deposit growth varied, with some banks struggling to keep pace with advances.
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Advance growth continued to outstrip deposit growth at several banks in the second quarter of FY27, with loan books expanding at a double-digit pace across public sector and mid-sized private lenders despite efforts to accelerate deposit mobilisation.
Provisional business updates for Q2FY27 show advances growing between 13% and 29% year-on-year across the banks, with smaller and regional lenders generally recording faster expansion than their larger peers. Tamilnad Mercantile Bank led the pack with 29.4% growth in advances, followed by Karnataka Bank at 24.9%, UCO Bank at 24.8% and J&K Bank at 23.7%.
Among larger public sector banks, Bank of India reported the fastest credit growth at 20.4%, followed by Canara Bank at 19.3%, Punjab & Sind Bank at 19.4%, Union Bank of India at 18.5% and Bank of Baroda at 18.3%. Punjab National Bank's advances grew 14.8%, while Indian Bank reported 16.6% growth.
Deposit growth, however, was more uneven. Bank of India's deposits rose 21.6%, ahead of its 20.4% credit growth, while Bank of Baroda's deposits grew 16.7%, broadly keeping pace with its 18.3% advance growth. Canara Bank's deposits rose 13.1% against 19.3% credit growth, while Union Bank's deposits grew 6.9% against 18.5% loan growth. 
At PNB, deposits grew 9.9%, compared with 14.8% growth in advances.
The divergence was more pronounced among some mid-sized lenders. UCO Bank's advances grew 24.8%, compared with 14.2% deposit growth, while J&K Bank reported 23.7% credit growth against 16.3% deposit growth. Karnataka Bank's advances rose 24.9%, more than twice the 12% growth in deposits.
Some lenders, however, managed to expand deposits faster than advances. Tamilnad Mercantile Bank's deposits grew 25.5%, compared with 29.4% growth in advances, while Dhanlaxmi Bank reported deposit growth of 20.2% against 22.3% credit growth. At South Indian Bank, both advances and deposits grew 18.7%.
The numbers point to continued pressure on banks to mobilise deposits even as credit demand remains firm.

briefs.headline: Anup Bagchi's Act 1: Set HDFC house in order
briefs.deck: Anup Bagchi has been chosen as the new CEO of HDFC Bank after Sashidhar Jagdishan's decision not to continue. Bagchi's leadership will address critical issues within the bank, including leadership succession and regulatory concerns. He aims to recapitalize the brand while focusing on technology and customer service improvements. Additionally, he encounters challenges with insurance sales amid…
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI/NEW DELHI: In late August, a day or two before Sashidhar Jagdishan announced his decision against seeking a fresh term, ICICI Life Insurance CEO Anup Bagchi received a call on his mobile. It was a surprise call from 
HDFC Bank
 chairman 
Rajiv Kumar
 and nomination and remuneration committee chair Harsh Bhanwala.
The trio discussed the developments in the financial sector and other issues before the ICICI veteran got a surprise offer, with the two HDFC Bank directors also informing him about a reference check having already been done with colleagues, peers and regulators. Bagchi is said to have laid down a few conditions, including informing his boss and long-time colleague Sandeep Bakhshi about the offer, lest he learn about it from someone else.
What followed was a fortnight of intense activity, including a video call that the HDFC Bank board had with Bagchi. His and deputy MD Kaizad Bahrucha's names went to RBI on August 12, with Kumar working to secure clearances before Sashi's Oct 26 exit. Bagchi's record helped. None of the businesses he led had faced regulatory penalties or admonitions, and he had served on RBI and Sebi panels.
Having tackled the public-sector banking crisis as financial services secretary in 2017, and later taken charge as chairman on June 29, the former chief election commissioner found HDFC Bank fundamentally sound but facing six issues: weak, divided leadership and succession planning; bond mis-selling in the UAE; MSRDC irregularities; a possible US class action; and the CFO's exit. 
Over the last three months, most of the issues have been addressed and the board is seen to be working together. It chose an outsider to help shift the group from an era shaped by towering personalities such as Aditya Puri and Deepak Parekh to one anchored in the institution.
Taking fresh guard
Bagchi's immediate priorities are recapitalising the brand and strengthening the leadership bench. Many seniors are set to retire and the "command culture" has resulted in the creation of satraps for each division.
The 55-year-old, currently designated additional director, has the task of breaking silos and putting the institution before individual ambition. He will also have to optimise the balance sheet by cutting high-cost liabilities, shedding assets to bring down the credit-deposit ratio, which stubbornly remains in the high 90s three years after the merger.
Technology and customer service are another area of focus. Bagchi also faces the delicate task of balancing HDFC Bank's aggressive insurance-sales culture with Irdai's tighter distribution rules, while retaining protection as an embedded offering for less-aware customers.

briefs.headline: RBI may end rate-cut cycle with first hike since February 2023
briefs.deck: Bankers expect the Reserve Bank of India to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points soon. This marks the end of the rate-cutting phase that began in February 2025. Economists predict inflation will exceed the RBI’s forecasts, necessitating tightening. Experts anticipate resilient growth will provide the RBI room to act despite external pressures. The focus will remain on managing liquidity and…
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: The era of falling interest rates that began in February 2025 is likely to end this week, with bankers and economists expecting RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points. The last increase came in February 2023, ending a tightening cycle that began after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
In February 2025, RBI cut rates by 25 basis points after a five-year pause, followed by 25bp in April, 50bp in June and 25bp in December, taking the repo rate to 5.25%.
It has held off on tightening despite inflation risks from the West Asia conflict and weaker farm output, betting that structural changes and stronger corporate and bank balance sheets could absorb margin pressure. SBI chairman CS Setty told TOI last week: "Our in-house view is that there could be a repo rate hike, but we do not expect it to materially impact credit growth," highlighting the resilience of the economy.
The impact may be felt faster in bank lending rates than in bonds, given the liquidity created by the FCNR(B) flows, which brought in $127 billion. That could push some borrowers towards the bond market. "On any shift towards bonds, much will depend on how market rates evolve, as bond yields have also moved up. 
Corporates today can move more seamlessly between bank borrowing and market funding, depending on relative pricing," Setty said.
Yes Bank
 chief economist Indranil Pan expects inflation to broaden, with Q2 inflation exceeding the RBI's 4.7% forecast and approaching 6% as higher input costs reach consumers. He sees resilient growth giving RBI room to tighten despite geopolitical risks, higher oil prices and rupee weakness, but expects the stance to remain neutral. "Given that there are signs of generalisation of price pressures, we expect RBI to start its hiking cycle in October by 25 bps," Pan said.
IndusInd Bank chief economist Gaurav Kapur puts the probability of a 25-basis-point October hike at 90%. Aastha Gudwani, India chief economist, expects the first hike on October 7, citing higher global oil prices and resilient domestic growth. "We expect terminal rate at 5.75%, with front-loaded hikes in Q4. Liquidity and monetary tightening to co-exist," she said.
Axis Capital chief economist Prateek Ancha expects a larger move. "Fed's latest rate hike and dot plot strengthen the case for 50bp of RBI tightening in CY26, split between October and December.
"We expect the overall hiking cycle to be limited to 75bp. In the near term, the RBI's focus is likely to remain on draining surplus liquidity and bringing overnight rates, currently 45bp below the policy rate, back in line with the policy rate."

briefs.headline: India in striking distance of 8% growth, says Shaktikanta Das
briefs.deck: India is expected to achieve close to 8% economic growth, aided by recent reforms and increased investment. The resilience of the economy is attributed to strategies implemented over the past decade and strong domestic demand. Former RBI governor Shaktikanta Das emphasized the significance of the financial sector and external management in supporting growth. Further opportunities are anticipated…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The Indian economy is within striking distance of 8% growth, on the back of GST and banking reforms, flexible inflation targeting, digital payments and fiscal prudence, a top PMO official said Sunday.
"Many of the reforms undertaken over the past decade were not designed as one-off measures, but as strategic buffers to enable the economy to absorb disruptions and recover rapidly," principal secretary to PM Shaktikanta Das said at the Kautilya Economic Conclave.
The Indian economy expanded 7.8% in the June quarter after a 7.9% growth last financial year and the former RBI governor attributed it to the strong domestic demand and investment. "India's resilience is not accidental. It is the outcome of broad and mutually reinforcing reforms," he said.
The former economic affairs secretary said India's financial sector and prudent management of the external sector had also emerged as strong pillars of economic growth. External sector indicators have remained broadly resilient, supported by export diversification, free trade agreements, a sustained surplus in services trade and steady inward remittances, he said.
Listing out a host of reforms undertaken by govt, Das said: "The journey ahead is focused on capitalising on the emerging opportunities."
Going forward, he said, the pace of activity will accelerate in five years, including AI, which can enhance productivity, improve public service delivery, accelerate scientific discovery, strengthen healthcare outcomes, and transform education.
He also called for deepening of the corporate bond market, pension and insurance funds, municipal finance and innovative infrastructure financing.

Under 
PM Narendra Modi
's vision, Next-generation GST was conceived with two connected purposes: to reduce and rationalise rates, and to make compliance easier. The rate changes took effect on Sept 22, 2025. The next phase of process reforms will come before the GST Council shortly. Together, these efforts seek to give households relief, businesses greater certainty and taxpayers a system in which they can fulfil their obligations without avoidable difficulty.
The states have been partners throughout. They brought their priorities and experience to the Council, helped shape the decisions and undertook their implementation. 
I thank them for that commitment. GST's progress rests on this willingness to pursue a shared national purpose while respecting each govt's responsibilities.
The results provide grounds for confidence. Between Oct 2025 and July 2026, the value of reported taxable supplies grew by 25.8% over the corresponding period a year earlier. A lighter rate structure has been accompanied by a substantial expansion in reported economic activity. This is an encouraging foundation for a reform intended to support both enterprise and public finances.
That resilience is visible in the latest revenue figures. Gross GST collections reached Rs 12.46 lakh crore during April-Sept 2026, up 11.6% over last year. Every month from June through Sept recorded double-digit annual growth; together, collections for these four months accelerated by nearly 15%. Net collections, after refunds, also grew by 10.4% over the half-year. Taxpayer relief has coexisted with growth in the resources available for development.
The breadth of the expansion matters as much as its scale. Reported taxable supplies grew across all 11 sector groups and all major states. Growth across sectors and regions creates opportunities for more businesses to participate in expanding markets, and for more communities to benefit from the demand, investment and employment that follow.
Reported sales to consumers (B2C) also rose by 26.7% in the post-reform comparison. When tax relief is reflected in prices, families have more room to meet other needs or save. Consumer relief and enterprise growth are closely connected: the purchasing power of households sustains demand for the goods and services that businesses provide.
For small and medium enterprises, a national market is valuable when it opens a practical route to customers beyond their immediate surroundings. Businesses in Tier-2 and Tier-3 towns should be able to build those relationships while continuing to invest and employ people locally. Enterprises expanding into these towns, in turn, can create opportunities for local suppliers and distributors. GST's common framework supports these connections; simpler administration must make them easier to sustain.
Participation in that framework is substantial. GST registrations across central and state jurisdictions stood at 1.7 crore at Aug-end, up nearly 15% from a year ago. During April-July, GSTR-3B returns filed by their due dates were 12.6% higher than a year ago. These improvements place a corresponding responsibility on the administration: regular compliance must be supported by reliable service, clear guidance and timely resolution of difficulties.
The functioning of input tax credit is another important part of this experience. The post-reform figures show that the share of tax liability discharged through credits rose, while accumulated credit declined relative to taxable supplies. This is encouraging for businesses that depend on the effective use of eligible credit. For a smaller firm, working capital determines how readily it can buy inputs, fulfil an order and take on the next one.
Refunds are equally relevant. Approximately Rs 1.8 lakh crore was refunded during April-Sept. Returning amounts due to businesses is part of a well-functioning tax system. Greater predictability in this process would help enterprises plan purchases and production with more confidence. The taxpayer's experience of receiving an eligible refund is an important measure of administrative performance.
The states also have a stronger revenue position. Their aggregate SGST receipts, including their share of IGST settlements, grew by about 16% during April-Sept. These resources support investment in infrastructure and public services. The gains can therefore reinforce one another: household relief supports demand, enterprise strengthens economic activity, and public revenues help sustain development.
The experience also points to the work ahead. A growing system must remain attentive to the costs it imposes on smaller participants. Their time and resources are limited. Each improvement in filing, credit or refunds should allow more of those resources to be devoted to running and expanding a business.
The proposals before the Council on Oct 7 have been developed through sustained work with the states. They address registration, returns, refunds, disputes and improved flow of input tax credit, with the aim of reducing the time and cost of compliance. Taxpayer experience must continue to guide implementation.
GST's growing maturity gives us a stronger foundation for the next stage of reform. The same commitment to clarity, certainty and respect for the taxpayer guides our work on direct taxes. A dependable tax system enables enterprises to plan beyond their immediate obligations and invest in opportunities that take time to mature. Giving them that confidence, wherever they operate, helps build the economic strength of a Viksit Bharat as envisioned by PM Narendra Modi.
(The author is Union finance and corporate affairs minister)

briefs.headline: GST Council meeting on October 7: Arrest powers, ITC, prosecution threshold proposals on agenda - report
briefs.deck: The GST Council will meet on October 7 to discuss major reforms in GST processes and enforcement. Proposed changes include removing tax officers' arrest powers and requiring judicial consent for any arrests. Additionally, the prosecution threshold may be raised from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore, with some offences being decriminalized. Changes are also aimed at simplifying compliance for small…
briefs.bodyText:
The GST Council may consider a package of GST process and enforcement reforms at its October 7 meeting, including a proposal to take away the power of tax officers to arrest taxpayers and require judicial authorisation for any arrest.
The Council may also consider raising the threshold for launching prosecution from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore and narrowing the scope of offences that can trigger criminal proceedings. Other proposals include protecting genuine buyers' input tax credit, easing GST registration for small e-commerce sellers and reducing low-value litigation, as per PTI sources.
The proposals are part of the government's next phase of GST reforms, with the focus shifting from rate rationalisation to simpler compliance, faster administration and more proportionate enforcement.
Arrest powers removed?
At the centre of the proposed changes is Section 69 of the Central GST Act, which allows the Commissioner to authorise an officer to arrest a person when statutory conditions are met and there are reasons to believe specified offences have been committed.
The proposal would remove this power from GST officials, with any arrest instead requiring judicial authorisation. Tax recovery, interest and financial penalties would continue to apply, while serious cases involving deliberate evasion or fraud could still be prosecuted through courts.
AMRG Global Managing Partner Rajat Mohan said the proposal marks a shift from arrest-led deterrence to technology-led detection. "With arrest removed and prosecution reserved for more serious cases, the focus is increasingly on using GSTN's data capabilities to detect fraud rather than relying on coercive powers," Mohan said.
Prosecution threshold may rise to Rs 5 crore
The Council is also likely to consider raising the prosecution threshold from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore.
"The threshold for prosecution is proposed to be raised from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore. That would reserve the criminal process for cases whose scale warrants it," a PTI source said.
The proposals seek to keep routine disputes over classification, valuation and input tax credit outside the criminal process. Of the 24 offences currently covered by prosecution provisions, nine are proposed to be removed, 11 retained and the remaining offences softened.
Input tax credit, e-commerce and litigation
Another proposal seeks to protect genuine buyers from losing input tax credit when an upstream supplier fails to pay tax. Under the proposal, recovery action would instead be directed at the defaulting seller.
The Council may also allow employers to claim ITC on premiums paid for employee insurance. Group insurance policies currently attract 18 per cent GST, which businesses cannot claim as credit.
For small e-commerce sellers, the Council may consider allowing platform warehouses to be used as registered places of business in states where sellers do not have their own premises. Sources said the move could help around 9.5 lakh small sellers access wider markets.
To reduce litigation, the Council may consider barring GST notices where the tax demand is below Rs 10,000. Such cases account for around 20 per cent of cases by number, according to the proposal.
Other proposals
The Council may also consider simpler GST registration and annual returns, quarterly tax payments for some MSMEs, intelligence-led checks on goods vehicles and a single 5 per cent GST rate without ITC for delivery of goods ordered through e-commerce platforms.
A separate proposal seeks to withdraw the IGST exemption available to banks and nominated agencies importing gold, silver and platinum.
The proposals are part of the broader GST 2.0 process reforms following the September 2025 rate rationalisation, which simplified the tax structure around 5 per cent and 18 per cent rates, with a 40 per cent rate for select luxury and demerit goods.

briefs.headline: Gold, silver lose lustre in September
briefs.deck: The firming up of the crude oil prices did not help the cause either
briefs.bodyText:
Precious metals lost their sheen in September with both gold and silver clocking negative returns last month. The strengthening of the U.S. Dollar and the expectations of interest rate hike in the U.S. dented the sentiment towards precious metals.
The firming up of the crude oil prices did not help the cause either.
As a result, Comex gold closed 6.8% lower to settle at $4,189.1 per ounce by the end of September. Comex silver suffered a relatively steeper cut of 9.6% to settle at $60.75/ounce.
Mirroring the global trend, precious metal prices settled at lower levels in the domestic markets too. The fall in the domestic market was, however, smothered by the weakening of the Indian Rupee against the U.S. Dollar.
MCX gold fell 4.1% in September to settle at ₹1,149,092/10 grams. MCX silver closed at ₹2,23,740/kilogram, representing a 6.8% fall last month.
Gold weaker
Contrary to expectations, Comex gold price remained weak last month and also breached the support zone of $4,200-$4,220 mentioned last month. As a result, the short-term outlook has been invalidated, and the price is likely to remain range bound and witness volatile price action in the $3,900-$4,550 range.
A definitive trend in Comex gold will emerge only if the price manages to breakout either above $4,560 or below $3,900. Expect lacklustre and range-bound price action to persist until either of the levels are taken out.
Similar to gold, Comex silver price, too, remained weak last month and also dropped below the support level of $62.5. The short-term uptrend has now been invalidated and price is likely to remain stuck in the broad range of $54 to $69 on the higher side. The price action is likely to be volatile and devoid of any meaningful trend until either of these levels are broken.
MCX gold price too drifted lower last month and breached the support level of ₹1,48,000. This has negated the positive outlook, and the price is now expected to oscillate in the ₹1,41,000-₹1,59,000 zone. Expect a yo-yo kind of price action within this zone to persist in the near future.
Similar to gold, the positive outlook for MCX silver price, too, has now been invalidated as the price dropped below the erstwhile support level of ₹2,25,000. Expect domestic silver price to remain range bound in the ₹2,15,000-₹2,48,000 range in the near term.
Conclusion
To summarise, the erstwhile positive short-term outlook for both gold and silver have been invalidated. Precious metal prices are likely to remain range bound until the levels mentioned above are not breached.
(The author is a Chennai based analyst / trader. The views and opinion featured in this column is based on the analysis of short-term price movement in gold and silver futures at COMEX & Multi Commodity Exchange of India. This is not meant to be a trading or investment advice.)
